articles.title: Anuvani-LID: Robust and Calibrated Spoken Language Identification for Indian Languages
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2610.20263v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Every multilingual speech pipeline begins with a language decision, an error there propagates silently through recognition, translation and routing. In India it spans 22 scheduled languages across four language families, heard over short, noisy, narrowband and code-mixed audio. Foundational speech models increasingly present language identification (LID) as an inherent latent, generalized capability. Autoregressive decoders in speech models emit a special language ID token, and modern LLMs with audio capabilities can name the language when prompted. We test this assumption on identical clips and find that whisper and similar speech models has tokens for only 15 of the 23 languages, on one second inputs Gemini 3.5 Flash reaches 0.52 macro-F1 and GPT-audio 0.14. We present Anuvani LID, a dedicated 115M parameter LID conformer model trained on 54,643 hours of Indian speech spanning 22 Indian languages and Indian accented English. Along with designed and controlled studies on 102 condition benchmark with speaker and corpus held out tests. Across 37 conditions, it reaches 0.914 mean macro-F1, 5.2 points above Gemini 3.5 Flash and ahead of 14 other systems. It is 24 points ahead of Gemini at one second, scores 0.897 on all 23 languages where no other system exceeds 0.713, and is calibrated to an ECE of 0.008. Reliable Indian LID still requires a robust, dedicated and calibrated model.

articles.title: Two Minds Better Than One: Collaborative Reward Modeling for LLM Alignment
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2505.10597v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reward models (RMs) are central to aligning large language models (LLMs) with human values, yet noisy preference feedback can induce reward misgeneralization through spurious correlations and overfitting. We characterize the training dynamics of preference pairs and uncover a distinctive optimization signature of noise: persistently high losses, sharp temporal fluctuations, and irregular gradient updates. Our analyses further show that excluding such pairs improves downstream alignment. In practice, however, reliable preferences are not known a priori, and self-filtering based on a model's own training signals can amplify confirmation bias. To address this challenge, we introduce Collaborative Reward Modeling (CRM), an online framework for identifying reliable preferences. CRM couples cross-model peer review with curriculum learning: two RMs evaluate each other's sample selections, while curriculum keeps their learning progress synchronized. Across extensive experiments, CRM improves RM generalization by up to 9.94 points on RewardBench under 40% preference noise. CRM further generalizes to implicit-reward alignment, offering a robust and broadly applicable approach to learning from imperfect feedback.

articles.title: AutoPrunedRetriever: Persistent Reasoning Graphs for Efficient and Extensible Retrieval-Augmented Generation
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2602.04926v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has become a standard approach for knowledge-intensive LLM tasks. Complex reasoning remains challenging because queries often require composing dispersed evidence through multiple dependent reasoning steps. Yet existing RAG systems process queries independently, repeatedly retrieving overlapping evidence and reconstructing established reasoning. Preserving such reasoning makes previously retrieved evidence and intermediate results reusable for subsequent queries. However, inference-time reuse becomes increasingly costly as the history grows, motivating a compact representation that preserves useful information without substantial loss in quality. To address these challenges, we present AutoPrunedRetriever (APR), a graph-based RAG system that encodes corpus facts and query-derived reasoning in a shared symbolic codebook. The codebook serves both as the retrieval index and as persistent memory, representing facts, questions, and answers as compact edge sequences, so that the previously established structure can be directly retrieved and reused. At inference time, APR retrieves query-specific reasoning paths and constructs compact prompts, while incremental consolidation keeps the growing memory compact. For deployments where the retriever cannot be replaced, we introduce AutoPruned Layer (APL), which leaves host retrieval unchanged but replaces the retrieved context with the corresponding entries in the shared symbolic codebook, writing each question and answer back as a compact structure. Across five complex-reasoning benchmarks, APR improves accuracy over the strongest baseline by 1.8-10.8 points while using up to 96% fewer input tokens. APL reduces generator input by 60-96% a

articles.title: Towards Reliable Truth-Aligned Uncertainty Estimation in Large Language Models
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2604.00445v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Uncertainty estimation (UE) aims to quantify uncertainty in large language model (LLM) outputs to flag potential hallucinations and support reliable deployment. However, UE metrics often exhibit unstable performance across models and datasets, limiting their practical utility. We formalise this phenomenon as proxy failure, arising because UE metrics are derived from model behaviour rather than being explicitly grounded in factual correctness. We show that when mutual information between a UE score and correctness is low, the score's discriminability must be close to chance. To address this, we propose Truth AnChoring (TAC), a lightweight post-hoc calibration method that maps raw UE scores to truth-aligned correctness probabilities. Even with noisy and few-shot supervision, TAC continues to improve calibration, providing a practical calibration protocol. Our findings highlight the limitations of treating heuristic UE metrics as direct indicators of uncertainty about factual correctness, and position our TAC as a principled step toward more reliable uncertainty estimation for LLMs. The code repository is available at https://github.com/ponhvoan/TruthAnchor/.

articles.title: HyperPersona: A Multi-Level Hypergraph Framework for Text-Based Automatic Personality Prediction
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2605.17355v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As a modern commodity, language has become a vast repository of socially and psychologically significant traits and concepts, reflecting the ways people encode pattern of thoughts, behaviors, and emotions into words. Text-based Automatic Personality Prediction (APP), seeks to infer personality from linguistic behavior, offering a scalable alternative to traditional psychometric assessments. Although text is inherently hierarchical, with the document-level capturing global features, the sentence-level encoding local semantics, and the word-level providing fine-grained lexical information, most existing approaches rely on shallow, sequential, or single-level representations that ignore the multi-level structure of written language. To address this, we propose HyperPersona, a framework that explicitly models the hierarchical organization of text (document, sentence, and word) through hypergraph structure, where a document and its sentences are represented as hyperedges, and the words are represented as nodes, enabling joint modeling of global, local, and lexical dependencies of text. Followed by a transformer-based graph encoder that learns interactions within and across these linguistic layers, yielding context-sensitive and structurally grounded feature representations for personality prediction. Experiments on the Big Five personality dimensions show that, while relying solely on text, HyperPersona effectively integrates multi-level linguistic cues, achieving superior performance compared to state-of-the-art baselines. These findings underscore the critical role of textual hierarchy in advancing human-like personality inference from natural language.

articles.title: Learning to Reason About Implicit Multimodal Harm: From Diagnosis to Generalization
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2605.29951v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A benign image paired with a benign caption can become harmful only in combination, making detection fundamentally a cross-modal reasoning problem. Existing multimodal harm benchmarks evaluate only classification accuracy, leaving unclear whether models identify the cross-modal mechanism that produces harm. We introduce MuPHI (Multimodal Pragmatic Harm Interpretation), a controlled diagnostic benchmark in which harm arises purely from image-text composition, with benign counterfactuals and annotated harm rationales. Using MuPHI, we systematically evaluate where compositional harm reasoning breaks in vision-language models (VLMs). MuPHI reveals that VLMs reliably ground each modality yet fail to bind the evidence into the harm mechanism and their predictions respond weakly to label-determining counterfactual interventions. Moreover, existing harm detection approaches trained on labels substantially improves in-domain (ID) detection but transfers poorly across harm distributions. We therefore propose Compositional Harm Interpretation Learning (CHIL), which rewards evidence identification in each modality, cross-modal binding and verdict consistency in the reasoning chain rather than just predicted label. CHIL improves 81% OOD transfer evaluations by an average of +2.5 macro-F1 and correct counterfactual flip rate by up to +3.8 and +5.4 % points, while also improving overall reasoning quality over label-only optimization. These results suggest that optimizing how a model reasons, not just what it concludes, offers a promising direction for multimodal safety systems that generalize beyond dataset-specific correlations.

articles.title: 中國捐贈「嫦娥六號」月壤樣品予聯合國 容啟亮：有重要象徵意義
articles.feed_excerpt: 國家早前將月球探測器「嫦娥六號」採集的首批月背月壤樣品贈予聯合國，在奧地利維也納辦事處永久展出。 理大深空探測研究中心主任容啟亮接受本台節目《看神州》訪問時說，國家捐贈樣品有重要象徵意義，代表願意去分享珍貴的航天成果，與不同國家和地區共享太空資源。透過深入分析研究採集到的樣品，可以證實以前對於月球的想法是否真實。 曾研製嫦娥六號「表取採樣執行裝置」的容啟亮表示，國家已經完成「繞、落、回」三個階段，下一步實現載人登月，在月球建設科研站，讓航天員有落腳點，以清楚進行測控工作，同時有助未來進一步探索火星。 他說，國家探月工作仍然面對很多挑戰，包括要確保航天員在月球安全著陸，以及有足夠的維生設備，亦要研究如何原地利用月球資源建設科研站等。 容啟亮又說，香港對國家和外國的運作都比較熟悉，加上本地不同跨學科的科研實力，可以助力國家實現航天夢。 編輯：汪溟曦

articles.title: 北京未來科技館體驗設施豐富參觀者感受深刻 冀助推動科研知識
articles.feed_excerpt: 位於延慶區世園內的北京未來科技館，十一黃金周前開館，國慶假期接待4萬多人，當中一半來自北京，其次多來自河北和天津。北京延慶區教委主任陶汪來相信，科技館為青少年提供沉浸體驗及作為探究科創實踐平台，有效補足校外科學教育短板，讓科學知識走出課本。 科技館樓高兩層，布展面積超過1萬平方米，有超過210個展覽項目。內設全亞洲首個穿戴式低重力模擬體驗館，廣東旅客汪小姐特地跟科技迷父親來體驗失重感覺。她說嘗試以單腳彈跳，發力越大彈得越高，落地力度亦會更大，體驗特別。 館內近9成半展覽貼合內地中小學生的科學課程，包括自然生態、基礎科學、數字科技、航天探索等，當中不少是體驗項目，包括體驗颱風威力、坐電梯模擬下沉到海洋世界，欣賞抹香鯨等海洋生物，認識國家研發的7000米級載人潛水器「蛟龍號」等。初中生王同學說，館內將課本圖片及文字資料變成體驗，印象深刻。 科技館成人收費60元，學生48元，北京世園研學文化發展有限公司總經理孟秀琴說，除了家庭客外，亦有來自南方的研學機構及團體預訂參觀，未來將持續深化「館校合作」，研發適合不同的科學研學課程，將研學資源輻射到北京市其他區。 編輯：黃佩珊

briefing.title: 乌克兰官员：美国必须施压俄罗斯以促使普京结束战争
briefing.summary: 乌克兰驻美副大使表示，美国必须向俄罗斯施压，以促使普京结束战争。报道称，在乌俄互相袭击之际，特朗普给予俄罗斯制裁豁免，扩大了他与泽连斯基的分歧。

briefing.title: 美国前官员：美中应借鉴冷战时期军控经验应对人工智能风险
briefing.summary: 美国前财政部长罗伯特·鲁宾呼吁华盛顿与北京搁置互不信任，应对人工智能带来的风险，并以上世纪美苏限制战略武器会谈等核军控合作作为先例。鲁宾曾在克林顿政府时期于1995年至1999年担任美国财政部长。

briefing.title: 抗日保台志士丘逢甲珍贵诗钞入藏中国人民抗日战争纪念馆
briefing.summary: 丘逢甲的侄曾孙丘嵩向中国人民抗日战争纪念馆捐赠《岭云海日楼诗钞》全四册。这套诗钞1936年定稿、1937年由国立中山大学铅印刊行，收录丘逢甲1895年至1911年间所作1700余首诗。

briefing.title: 深度伪造、机器人与不信任：人工智能如何影响以色列选举
briefing.summary: 人工智能首次在以色列选举中发挥重要作用。观察人士警告，深度伪造、机器人和影响行动可能左右选民。

briefing.title: 伯纳姆被敦促调查空气污染健康影响的不平等
briefing.summary: 据标题及摘要，150名科学家、议员和活动人士联名呼吁就空气污染的不平等影响展开调查；摘要称财政研究所研究显示，英格兰低收入地区空气污染水平持续高于富裕地区。

briefing.title: 基辅称俄中美元首峰会只会延长战争
briefing.summary: 乌克兰外长瑟比加周一表示，俄罗斯、中国和美国举行峰会会鼓励普京延长战争。据《华尔街日报》报道，普京提议下月与美国总统特朗普、中国国家主席习近平举行峰会，按有利于莫斯科的条件谈判结束战争。

briefing.title: NASA改进冲击与振动分析
briefing.summary: 火箭升空时会产生强烈振动、晃动和弯曲，搭载精密科学仪器的航天器必须承受这些力量。NASA工程师在火箭发射前努力预测这些应力将如何影响航天器各部件；动态环境小组的工程师为此开展相关工作。

briefing.title: 俄罗斯的拉夫罗夫访问德黑兰 讨论美国战争与地区安全
briefing.summary: 据标题与摘要，俄罗斯的拉夫罗夫在访问德黑兰期间讨论美国战争和地区安全；海湾合作委员会国家已敦促莫斯科帮助停止伊朗袭击并重新开放霍尔木兹海峡。
